subject: Finding related nodes by parameter names

messages.author: 6cf4f730b8d1254e
messages.subject: Finding related nodes by parameter names
parts:
Hello all,

While trying to code up a sampler from JAGS's glm factory in Nimble, I hit a little snag. For a problem of the form y ~ f(mu), g^-1(mu) = \eta = XB + Z \Gamma with Z stochastic and X data/deterministic, is there a straightforward way to retrieve X and Z from the model object or graph given the parameter names for B and \Gamma?

As far as I can tell, the products of XB and Z \Gamma are not necessarily stored in a node (besided \eta), which (seemingly) makes this a little more challenging.

Kind regards,
Bert

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Finding related nodes by parameter names
parts:
Bert, I'm sure there's a way to do what you'd like to do.  That said, I'm having a hard time making sense of your question.

Just as written, it seems you could use model_object$X or model_object$Z to retrieve X or Z from the model object, neither of which require the parameter names for B or \Gamma.  So again, I don't think I'm following the question.

Or, is it perhaps the X and Z are only calculated as variables internal to your custom sampler?  Is that it?

Perhaps you could provide a snippet of code, which might help elucidate the issue you're up against?

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Finding related nodes by parameter names
parts:
I'm not sure but I think you're asking how to symbolically process content from model declarations, e.g. how to access the expression XB + Z \Gamma from a model declaration and symbolically determine that what multiplies B is X.

We don't really have tools for that. You can get a list of internal pieces from a model declaration that include the pieces you would need to get started by model$getDeclInfo(node). For example, see the "valueExpr" field of the object returned by model$getDeclInfo. From there you would need to write the symbolic processing yourself.

If I follow what you are interested in creating, it would be quite interesting and is something we've thought about at times, so please do reach out to share any progress.

Best wishes
Perry

Thanks both, apologies for poorly formulating my question. Perry's interpretation was spot on.

@Daniel, in a quite general setting, in a GLM(M) a user might call "Z" or "X" whatever they would like, hence I cannot rely on being able to pull those quantities straight from the model object.

According to Bob O'Hara,  BUGS was able to retrieve such connections by (quote:) "going up and down the graph". Anyhow, I will take a look at Perry his suggestions and report back if I manage to construct something.

Kind regards,
Bert
